title: Sunrise Clinic POC scoping - quality eval plan
customer_attendees: Dr. Lee Kim - Director Clinical Ops
summary: POC scoping focused on the quality evaluation plan for Sunrise Clinic's clinical note summarization and triage assistant. Discussed success criteria (accuracy, hallucination rate, format adherence), workload sizing, benchmark plan, golden prompt set, regression tests, scoring approach (weighted metrics), and timeline for a 4-week pilot. Security and data residency questions flagged; Redwood to share SOC2 and eval templates.
topics: Golden prompts and test set construction

Priya to run initial baseline on hosted API and share latency report by 2026-04-22
Schedule technical deep dive with infra team w/c 2026-04-27
Alex to send pricing + draft SOW by 2026-04-24

Sam Torres - Send security contact and list of required compliance docs - due 2026-04-21

transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick round of intros, i'm Alex from Redwood, priya our se, omar csm. 
[00:10] Jordan (Sunrise - VP Product): Jordan here, Lee, Maya, Sam on from our side. good to be here.
[00:18] Priya (SE): Awesome. Objective for today: nail down the quality eval plan for the POC — golden prompts, regression tests, what success looks like.
[00:25] Dr. Lee (Customer): Right, the main ask is clinical note summarization with triage flags. accuracy is critical, also zero hallucinations ideally for things like medications.
[00:36] Maya (Head of AI): To add, we need structured outputs in FHIR-ish JSON, and some downstream parsers are strict so format adherence matters.
[00:45] Alex: Great, so high level success criteria we usually track: accuracy / clinical fidelity, hallucination rate, format correctness, latency/throughput for our worst-case sequences. Any other must-haves?
[00:56] Sam (Security): Data retention and encryption at rest + in transit, and SSO/SAML for access. Also need SOC2 and audit logs.
[01:05] Alex: Yep will share SOC2. We support SAML + RBAC, and for POC we can do hosted but we also have private/VPC options if you need.
[01:15] Jordan: Timeline thoughts? We want a pilot that runs fast, 3-4 weeks ideally.
[01:20] Priya: That aligns. Our typical POC is 4 weeks: week 0 ingest + baseline, week 1 run golden set and iterate, week 2 regression / robustness, week 3 finalize scoring and handoff.
[01:31] Dr. Lee: How big should the golden set be?
[01:34] Priya: For clinical summarization we recommend 300-1,000 golden examples covering common and edge cases. Practically we ask for 500 de-identified notes + ~50 edge/medical-error cases and 50 format-edge samples.
[01:46] Maya: We can produce 500, plus a set of 60 edge cases. Concern: de-id tooling sometimes strips context which affects model outputs.
[01:54] Alex: Noted. We'll accept de-id exports but ask you annotate if critical PHI removal changes clinical intent.
[02:02] Jordan: What about metrics? Exact match seems too strict.
[02:06] Priya: Agreed. We propose a weighted scoring approach: 50% clinical fidelity (measured by clinician ratings on a 0-5 scale and a strict medication/diagnosis exactness check), 20% hallucination penalty (percentage of outputs containing unsupported facts), 20% format/JSON schema adherence, 10% latency (p95 under target). We'll produce an aggregated score 0-100 and pass threshold say 80.
[02:28] Dr. Lee: How do you measure hallucinations?
[02:31] Priya: Combination: automated heuristics (named-entity cross-check with source notes) plus manual reviewer flags on a sample of 200 outputs. Hallucination rate target <= 2% for pass.
[02:42] Maya: Manual review will be the bottleneck, how many labels?
[02:45] Alex: We usually do stratified sampling: 200 random + 100 edge cases labeled by clinicians for the POC. We can provide a review dashboard link.
[02:55] Jordan: Benchmarks vs what? You mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI earlier.
[03:00] Priya: We'll run baselines on the hosted Redwood API against a matched open model baseline; we can also include your in-house model if you share docker or endpoint. Competitor mentions are for context only.
[03:10] Sam: Any concerns about PII leaking in logs?
[03:13] Alex: For the POC we can enable strict log redaction and disable retention beyond 14 days, or do a private deployment if needed. We'll note that in the SOW.
[03:23] Dr. Lee: On workload sizing: our peak is about 30 requests/min for summarization but batch processing overnight can be thousands.
[03:31] Priya: Ok that maps to two modes: interactive (low latency p95 target 300ms) and batch (throughput target 500 notes/min). We'll tune batching and KV cache for your distribution.
[03:42] Anu (Data Eng): Typical note lengths are 600-1,200 tokens, with some up to 3k.
[03:47] Priya: That's helpful — sequence length affects kernel choice and latency. We'll include quantization profiles recommendation if cost becomes a concern.
[03:55] Jordan: Tell us about regression tests — how do they plug into our CI?
[03:59] Priya: We provide a regression harness: you maintain a test set (golden + negative cases) in the eval sheet. On every model update or prompt change we run the suite and produce diffs; failing thresholds can block rollout. We can output results as JSON or CSV for your CI.
[04:14] Maya: Can we automate hallucination checks in CI?
[04:17] Priya: To an extent — entity cross-checks, schema validation, and fuzzy-string matching can be automated. Human review remains for subtle clinical hallucinations.
[04:26] Dr. Lee: About golden prompts — do you curate them or do we?
[04:29] Alex: Collaboration is best. Redwood will seed with 50 canonical prompts and examples; you augment with clinical edge prompts. We'll ask for a 'golden prompt set' of 30 high-priority prompts that must be robust.
[04:40] Jordan: How are prompts versioned?
[04:42] Priya: We keep prompt and model versioning in the eval spreadsheet; each run is tagged with model id, prompt id, and timestamp so you can roll back.
[04:50] Sam: If we go to Private/VPC for POC, how long to set up?
[04:54] Alex: VPC private control plane typically 2-3 weeks including networking and keys; for the POC we're aiming hosted unless security requires otherwise.
[05:02] Anu: For the de-id export, what's the preferred format?
[05:05] Priya: CSV with note_id, raw_text (de-id), length_tokens, and reference_summary if available. Also a small JSON file for edge-case annotations.
[05:14] Jordan: On scoring: you mentioned clinician ratings. Who organizes?
[05:18] Alex: We can provide a labeling UI and instructions; you supply clinicians. We'll host the UI or you can run it locally. We'll also provide a rubric template.
[05:27] Maya: Cost — what's the expected compute for 500 notes?
[05:30] Priya: For hosted baseline using a 16GB model, 500 notes at avg 1k tokens is roughly couple of hours using batching; cost estimate will be in the eval spreadsheet. If you need dedicated GPUs or quantized models, costs shift but throughput improves.
[05:43] Jordan: Any other risks?
[05:44] Priya: Biggest risks: de-id affecting clinical fidelity, insufficient edge-case coverage, and model hallucinations on rare conditions. Mitigations: targeted edge-case set, manual review, and fallback policies for unknowns.
[05:57] Dr. Lee: For fallback, can we return "unable to summarize" vs a hallucinated summary?
[06:01] Alex: Yes - we can tune the system to return conservative answers or a confidence score and label uncertain outputs for human review.
[06:08] Sam: Audit logs and key management?
[06:11] Alex: We support KMS integrations and provide audit logs for requests; we'll include that in the security pack.
[06:20] Jordan: ok let's recap and confirm deadlines.
[06:24] Alex: Recap: Sunrise provides 500 de-id notes + 60 edge cases by 2026-04-25; Maya to coordinate. Priya runs baseline and shares latency by 2026-04-22. Alex will share eval spreadsheet, golden prompts, SOC2, and draft SOW by 2026-04-20. We target pilot start 2026-04-27.
[06:44] Maya: Sounds good.
[06:46] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll sync weekly.
[06:50] Alex: Thanks, meeting over.
